passages.text: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, To Philemon our beloved fellow worker, to Apphia our sister, to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets at your house: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a prisoner for Christ Jesus.
Timothy is our brother.
We write to Philemon.
Philemon is our beloved fellow worker.
We also write to Apphia.
Apphia is our sister.
We also write to Archippus.
Archippus is our fellow soldier.
We also write to the church that meets in your house.
We pray for grace for you.
We pray for peace for you.
Grace and peace come from God our Father.
Grace and peace come from the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: Παῦλος δέσμιος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ Τιμόθεος ὁ ἀδελφὸς Φιλήμονι τῷ ἀγαπητῷ καὶ συνεργῷ ἡμῶν καὶ Ἀπφίᾳ τῇ ἀδελφῇ καὶ Ἀρχίππῳ τῷ συστρατιώτῃ ἡμῶν καὶ τῇ κατ’ οἶκόν σου ἐκκλησίᾳ Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: I always thank my God, remembering you in my prayers, because I hear about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter.
Paul is a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
Paul writes with Timothy, his brother in Christ.
Paul writes to Philemon.
Philemon is a beloved fellow worker.
Paul always thanks his God.
Paul remembers Philemon in his prayers.
Paul hears about Philemon’s faith in the Lord Jesus.
Paul hears about Philemon’s love for all the saints.
passages.original: Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ Θεῷ μου πάντοτε μνείαν σου ποιούμενος ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου ἀκούων σου τὴν ἀγάπην καὶ τὴν πίστιν ἣν ἔχεις πρὸς τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν καὶ εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους

passages.text: I pray that your partnership in the faith may become effective as you fully acknowledge every good thing that is ours in Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
Paul writes to Philemon, Apphia, Archippus, and the church in Philemon’s house.
Paul prays for Philemon.
Paul wants Philemon’s partnership in the faith to become effective.
Paul asks God to help Philemon fully recognize every good thing that belongs to believers in Christ.
Paul wants Philemon to know all the good things that are in Christ.
passages.original: ὅπως ἡ κοινωνία τῆς πίστεώς σου ἐνεργὴς γένηται ἐν ἐπιγνώσει παντὸς ἀγαθοῦ τοῦ ἐν ἡμῖν εἰς Χριστόν

passages.text: I take great joy and encouragement in your love, because you, brother, have refreshed the hearts of the saints.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Paul writes to his Christian brother.
Paul feels great joy.
Paul receives encouragement.
Paul feels this joy and encouragement because of his brother’s love.
Paul’s brother has shown love to the saints.
Paul’s brother has refreshed the hearts of the saints.
Paul calls him “brother.”
passages.original: χαρὰν γὰρ πολλὴν ἔσχον καὶ παράκλησιν ἐπὶ τῇ ἀγάπῃ σου ὅτι τὰ σπλάγχνα τῶν ἁγίων ἀναπέπαυται διὰ σοῦ ἀδελφέ

passages.text: So although in Christ I am bold enough to order you to do what is proper, I prefer to appeal on the basis of love. For I, Paul, am now aged, and a prisoner of Christ Jesus as well.
passages.sermon:
I am Paul.
I am now an old man.
I am also a prisoner for Christ Jesus.
In Christ, I have great boldness.
I could command you to do what is right.
But I choose to appeal to you because of love.
passages.original: Διό πολλὴν ἐν Χριστῷ παρρησίαν ἔχων ἐπιτάσσειν σοι τὸ ἀνῆκον διὰ τὴν ἀγάπην μᾶλλον παρακαλῶ τοιοῦτος ὢν ὡς Παῦλος πρεσβύτης νυνὶ δὲ καὶ δέσμιος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whose father I became while I was in chains.
passages.sermon:
I am Paul.
I am now old.
I am a prisoner for Christ Jesus.
I appeal to you.
I appeal to you about Onesimus.
Onesimus is my child in the faith.
I became his spiritual father while I was in chains.
passages.original: Παρακαλῶ σε περὶ τοῦ ἐμοῦ τέκνου ὃν ἐγέννησα ἐν τοῖς δεσμοῖς Ὀνήσιμον

passages.text: Formerly he was useless to you, but now he has become useful both to you and to me.
passages.sermon: Onesimus was once useless to you.\r\nNow Onesimus is useful to you.\r\nNow Onesimus is also useful to me.
passages.original: τόν ποτέ σοι ἄχρηστον νυνὶ δὲ καὶ σοὶ καὶ ἐμοὶ εὔχρηστον

passages.text: I am sending back to you him who is my very heart.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter while he is in prison.
Paul speaks to Philemon.
Paul refers to Onesimus.
Paul calls Onesimus his own child.
Paul says, "I am sending Onesimus back to you."
Paul says, "Onesimus is my very heart."
passages.original: ὃν ἀνέπεμψά σοι αὐτόν τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τὰ ἐμὰ σπλάγχνα

passages.text: I would have liked to keep him with me, so that on your behalf he could minister to me in my chains for the gospel.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing this letter.
Paul is in prison for preaching the gospel.
Paul is speaking about Onesimus.
I wanted to keep Onesimus with me.
I am in chains for the gospel.
Onesimus could serve me while I am in prison.
He would serve me on your behalf.
passages.original: ὃν ἐγὼ ἐβουλόμην πρὸς ἐμαυτὸν κατέχειν ἵνα ὑπὲρ σοῦ μοι διακονῇ ἐν τοῖς δεσμοῖς τοῦ εὐαγγελίου

passages.text: But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your goodness will not be out of compulsion, but by your own free will.
passages.sermon:
I did not want to act without your permission.
I wanted your kindness to be voluntary.
I did not want your goodness to be forced.
I wanted you to choose to do good freely.
passages.original: Χωρὶς δὲ τῆς σῆς γνώμης οὐδὲν ἠθέλησα ποιῆσαι ἵνα μὴ ὡς κατὰ ἀνάγκην τὸ ἀγαθόν σου ᾖ ἀλλὰ κατὰ ἑκούσιον

passages.text: For perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while, so that you might have him back for good— no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a beloved brother. He is especially beloved to me, but even more so to you, both in person and in the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Onesimus was your slave.
He was separated from you for a short time.
Perhaps God allowed this to happen for a reason.
Now you can have him back forever.
You will not have him as a slave anymore.
You will have him as more than a slave.
You will have him as a beloved brother.
He is very dear to me.
He will be even dearer to you.
He will be dear to you both as a person and as a brother in the Lord.
passages.original: τάχα γὰρ διὰ τοῦτο ἐχωρίσθη πρὸς ὥραν ἵνα αἰώνιον αὐτὸν ἀπέχῃς οὐκέτι ὡς δοῦλον ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ δοῦλον ἀδελφὸν ἀγαπητόν μάλιστα ἐμοί πόσῳ δὲ μᾶλλον σοὶ καὶ ἐν σαρκὶ καὶ ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: So if you consider me a partner, receive him as you would receive me.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul is an apostle and a Christian leader.
Paul writes to Philemon.
Paul asks Philemon to accept Onesimus.
Paul says, "If you think of me as your partner, accept Onesimus."
Paul says, "Welcome him as you would welcome me."
passages.original: Εἰ οὖν με ἔχεις κοινωνόν προσλαβοῦ αὐτὸν ὡς ἐμέ

passages.text: But if he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer of this letter.
Paul speaks to Philemon.
Paul refers to Onesimus, who was once a slave to Philemon.
Paul says, "If Onesimus has wronged you in any way, charge it to me."
Paul also says, "If Onesimus owes you anything, put that on my account."
passages.original: εἰ δέ τι ἠδίκησέν σε ἢ ὀφείλει τοῦτο ἐμοὶ ἐλλόγα

passages.text: I, Paul, write this with my own hand. I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me your very self.
passages.sermon:
I am Paul.
I write this with my own hand.
I will repay what is owed.
You also owe me your very self.
passages.original: ἐγὼ Παῦλος ἔγραψα τῇ ἐμῇ χειρί ἐγὼ ἀποτίσω ἵνα μὴ λέγω σοι ὅτι καὶ σεαυτόν μοι προσοφείλεις

passages.text: Yes, brother, let me have some benefit from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Philemon.
Paul calls Philemon "brother."
Paul asks Philemon for a benefit.
Paul wants this benefit in the Lord.
Paul says, "Let me have some benefit from you in the Lord."
Paul asks Philemon to refresh his heart.
Paul wants his heart refreshed in Christ.
passages.original: Ναί ἀδελφέ ἐγώ σου ὀναίμην ἐν Κυρίῳ ἀνάπαυσόν μου τὰ σπλάγχνα ἐν Χριστῷ

passages.text: Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I ask.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter.
Paul feels confident in your obedience.
Paul knows you will do what he asks.
Paul believes you will do even more than he asks.
passages.original: Πεποιθὼς τῇ ὑπακοῇ σου ἔγραψά σοι εἰδὼς ὅτι καὶ ὑπὲρ ἃ λέγω ποιήσεις

passages.text: In the meantime, prepare a guest room for me, because I hope that through your prayers I will be restored to you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul is an apostle.
Paul writes to a Christian brother.
Paul asks the brother to prepare a guest room for him.
Paul hopes to visit the brother.
Paul believes the brother and the church pray for him.
Paul hopes God will answer their prayers.
Paul hopes God will allow him to come to them.
passages.original: Ἅμα δὲ καὶ ἑτοίμαζέ μοι ξενίαν ἐλπίζω γὰρ ὅτι διὰ τῶν προσευχῶν ὑμῶν χαρισθήσομαι ὑμῖν

passages.text: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings, as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
passages.sermon:
Epaphras sends you greetings.
Epaphras is my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus.
Mark sends you greetings.
Aristarchus sends you greetings.
Demas sends you greetings.
Luke sends you greetings.
Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke are my fellow workers.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζεταί σε Ἐπαφρᾶς ὁ συναιχμάλωτός μου ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ Μᾶρκος Ἀρίσταρχος Δημᾶς Λουκᾶς οἱ συνεργοί μου

passages.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
passages.sermon: The Lord Jesus Christ gives grace.\r\nThis grace is with your spirit.
passages.original: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματος ὑμῶν
